correctness.rationale: For n=3,4,5,6 every claimed rational circulant matrix is certified by exact coefficient identity (12I−6hQ+h²Q²)N(h)=D(h)(12I+6hQ+h²Q²). All denominator factors are positive; every required numerator on n≤5 is positive at h>0. For n6 only the nearest-neighbor numerator −2hF6 changes sign, and Descartes’ one-positive-root argument is decisive. The periodic Laplacian pseudoinverse Green kernel is independently proved via cyclic second differences and zero row sums, yielding the explicit negative leading coefficient for all n≥6. The scalar R(−t)=(t²−6t+12)/(t²+6t+12) belongs to (0,1) for t>0, proving simultaneous spectral stability and mass conservation. Exact rational h=7 witness checked. The universal n claim is analytical, not extrapolated from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The direct full text of early Padé positive-system papers establishes generic positivity failures and sufficient bounds, while classical absolute-monotonicity theory establishes a universal RK obstruction. Neither located full-text statement classifies the periodic nearest-neighbor cycle by size, identifies the exact six-cycle quartic, or derives the all-size failure coefficient from the cycle Laplacian pseudoinverse. Publicly indexed related findings on eight-state pure-birth small-step failure and filtered-CN cycle positivity are genuinely different. The own-history comparison specifically excludes a preexisting four-vertex path cutoff and four-cycle special case; the new theorem is instead the five/six-cycle and all-cycle classification. Older cyclic-matrix positivity results remain a possible residual risk.
residual_risks: An older circulant rational-matrix or Fourier-grid positivity paper may encode the same six-cycle threshold under different terminology.
The full 1998 Horváth RK positivity paper was not obtained; no claim of whole-document noncoverage is made.
The asymptotic all-size law is sharp for fixed cycle n, not uniform in n; the exact positivity set for cycles n≥7 remains unclassified here.

value.rationale: The nearest-neighbor periodic lattice is a canonical conservative semidiscretization of diffusion, and a numerical propagator must be nonnegative to represent a stochastic transition. The result supplies an all-size yes/no classification of unconditional positivity, a sharp first failing finite mesh and explicit threshold, and an exact Green-function mechanism explaining why the graph-size boundary is six despite unconditional A-stability and all-step positivity through five sites. This is a motivated natural classification and practical maximum safe step, not an arbitrary isolated matrix entry or a routine consequence of generic SSP radii.
